public_body: Massachusetts Auto Damage Appraiser Licensing Board
overall: Board violated the OML by discussing the Steere complaints in its October 4 executive session under the quasi-judicial exception, which applies only after an Order to Show Cause issues. No intentional violation found; minutes to be amended.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board entered executive session for an improper purpose on October 4 when discussing a complaint against a licensed appraiser under the quasi-judicial exception.
allegations.key_passage: The Board could not invoke the quasi-judicial exception because the adjudicatory process had not yet begun as the Board had not issued an Order to Show Cause but simply discussed a proposed draft order.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to give the complainant 48 hours' written notice that he would be discussed in the October 4 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The individual must be notified in writing by the public body at least 48 hours prior to the proposed executive session.

allegations.summary: Challenge to the October 4 executive session as a whole, including discussions of an applicant and two other licensees' complaints under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: the Board properly met in executive session and afforded the individuals their rights under Purpose 1.

remedy: Amend the October 4 executive session minutes to include the omitted discussion between the Board and Legal Counsel about the legal elements of the Order to Show Cause.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
